headline: Oil near 113 dollars, rate hike bets build, and Jio's final day

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the twenty-third of October, and this is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, oil. Brent crude has climbed to a five-month high of around 113 dollars a barrel after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, and that pushed Indian shares lower for a third straight session. Second, interest rates. The minutes of the Reserve Bank's last policy meeting have convinced economists that two more rate hikes are coming, in December and February. And third, it's the last day to bid in the Jio Platforms IPO, which has already drawn demand of about 3.7 lakh crore rupees.

Add to that a packed results day, with Infosys, Dr Reddy's and JSW Steel reporting, and three new listings this morning. Let's begin.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Thursday was another tough session. The Sensex lost over 460 points, and the Nifty fell 124 points, or just over half a percent, to 22,687. Oil-sensitive stocks led the decline as Brent crossed 112 dollars, and companies listed on the BSE lost about 3 lakh crore rupees in market value in a single day. Both indices are now down about 2 percent this week.

Now to the money flows. Provisional data show foreign institutional investors sold a net 3,459 crore rupees of Indian shares on Thursday, while domestic institutions bought 2,891 crore rupees. So far this year, foreign investors have sold a net 4.57 lakh crore rupees, and domestic institutions have bought 6.93 lakh crore.

Among individual names, eMudhra hit a second straight 20 percent lower circuit after a leak of private keys tied to its web security certificates. The IT ministry has formed a special team to investigate. And Swiggy hit a record low, down 46 percent from its IPO price, ahead of results the market found disappointing.

For today, GIFT Nifty points to a firmer start, trading around 22,800, about 165 points above Thursday's futures close. Analysts quoted by Moneycontrol see resistance in the 22,800 to 22,900 zone, and crucial support at 22,500. A break below that, they say, could drag the index towards 22,200 to 22,300. For Bank Nifty, the level they're watching is 54,400.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
Three companies make their stock market debut today. Zetwerk Manufacturing, whose 5,012 crore rupee IPO combined new shares worth 2,830 crore with a sale by existing holders. Bonfiglioli Transmissions, with an issue of about 2,534 crore rupees, all of it a sale by existing shareholders. And Sahajanand Medical Technologies, a 475 crore rupee issue, also entirely a sale by existing holders. On Thursday, Fusion CX listed at 305 rupees, a premium of about five and a half percent to its issue price of 289 but closed almost flat.

One date for your calendar. Bombay Coated and Special Steels opens a 183 crore rupee IPO on the twenty-ninth of October.

On deals, the Swiss bank UBS has taken a 4.8 percent stake in 360 ONE WAM by exercising warrants, over a year after it moved its Indian wealth business to the firm. And Sun Pharma raised 7,816 crore rupees through two five-year bonds, with coupons of 8.05 and 8.2 percent.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to results. In metals, Jindal Stainless grew profit 11 percent to 898 crore rupees in the September quarter, but cut its volume growth outlook for this financial year to 4 to 6 percent, from 7 to 9 percent earlier. Hindustan Petroleum's profit fell 6 percent, even as revenue rose 26 percent. It's back in profit after a heavy loss in the June quarter, but still in the red for the half-year because of high crude prices.

In finance, CreditAccess Grameen's profit jumped fourfold to 502 crore rupees, helped by lower credit costs, and it raised its profitability guidance. Its assets under management grew 19.5 percent. On the other side, M&M Financial reported a 55 percent jump in profit, yet the stock fell as much as 10 percent to a 52-week low, as brokerages cut their targets over margin pressure, higher funding costs and risks to rural cash flows.

In consumer goods, Colgate-Palmolive posted a 4.2 percent rise in profit to 342 crore rupees, on revenue growth of 12.2 percent, and declared a dividend of 24 rupees a share.

Today brings the big ones. Analysts quoted by Business Standard expect Infosys's profit to rise about 10 percent, with the focus on any change to its revenue guidance for the year. For JSW Steel, analysts see adjusted profit growing 60 to 110 percent from a year ago. Dr Reddy's also reports.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
The Reserve Bank's minutes have shifted expectations. Economists now expect a quarter-point hike in both December and February, and don't rule out a third in April if crude stays above 100 dollars. Barclays says the chance of a December hike has gone up, and now sees rates peaking at 6 percent in this cycle. Former Governor C Rangarajan told Moneycontrol that India faces a two-fold problem of inflation and the rupee, and the tightening may have to be stronger.

Cash is getting tight too. The banking system's liquidity surplus shrank to just 541 crore rupees as of the twenty-first, and the overnight call rate rose to 5.65 percent, 15 basis points above the repo rate.

The oil bill tells the story. India's crude import bill rose 46 percent to 90.6 billion dollars between April and September. The Indian crude basket has averaged about 121 dollars a barrel this October, against 65 dollars a year ago. India is also buying more from West Asia, which supplied 54 percent of its crude in September, while Russian imports fell.

Now, tax. Two GST changes arrive on the first of November. Small e-commerce sellers get simplified registration, and can declare an e-commerce warehouse as their principal place of business, so they can sell across states without physical offices. Refunds will be issued automatically, and a minimum threshold for show-cause notices should cut litigation. Separately, the government plans to revamp GST return forms to curb mismatches between reported sales and tax paid. Draft forms open for public feedback from the first of November, with the changes taking effect on the first of April 2027.

On trade, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said the India and European Union trade pact should be signed by the end of this year, and could be in force between January and March.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Wall Street had a rough night. The Nasdaq fell 2.6 percent, its steepest drop since early June, as investors dumped artificial intelligence stocks. Meta slid over 6 percent after raising its spending plans to as much as 145 billion dollars, despite strong revenue.

Brent crude is little changed this morning at about 113 dollars, after a 4 percent surge, on supply worries following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. Asian shares are lower, with the broad regional index heading for a fourth straight weekly loss. Gold is holding near a three-month low, around 4,110 dollars an ounce, as investors sell it to cover losses elsewhere.

In China, growth rebounded faster than expected, with industrial output up 5.5 percent in September. And memory chip maker Solidigm scrapped a 10 billion dollar IPO, dragging SK Hynix down 3 percent.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the Jio IPO you're following. On day two, the offer was subscribed 5.57 times. Big institutions bid for 13.29 times their quota, wealthy individuals for nearly six times, and retail investors for 1.54 times, so the retail portion is now full. Moneycontrol puts total demand at about 3.73 lakh crore rupees. Bidding closes today, with allotment expected on Monday and listing next Wednesday.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Now, your money. The market regulator, Sebi, has warned investors about invitation-only WhatsApp groups that hand out stock tips in the name of free education. It flagged fake profit claims, planted messages, overseas numbers and suspicious trading apps, and urged investors to deal only with registered intermediaries.

Some relief for traders. From the twenty-second of February 2027, clients who deliver shares early can use that value for later trades without putting up extra margin.

If you bank with ICICI, note that charges on cash transactions beyond the free limit, on demand drafts and on returned auto-debits change from the first of December. The free monthly limits stay the same. Indian Bank has raised rates on its 555-day and 777-day special deposits by 15 basis points from today, following the Reserve Bank's October rate hike.

On Yes Bank's additional tier one bonds, after the Supreme Court reversed the 8,415 crore rupee write-down, sources say the bank is unlikely to pay coupons this year, insisting the decision is its own to make.

And one win for policyholders. Delhi's state consumer commission rejected HDFC ERGO's appeal over a dengue claim of nearly 18 lakh rupees, ruling that a two-year waiting period didn't apply because dengue wasn't on the list of specified illnesses.

That's the brief for this Friday. Today, watch whether the Nifty can hold 22,500 and end its three-day slide, how Zetwerk, Bonfiglioli and Sahajanand open, and the final day of bidding for Jio. After the bell come Infosys, Dr Reddy's and JSW Steel, and keep one eye on crude through it all. Have a good weekend.
